HTTP/3. The engine's options are in [Ktor: Server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#server) and the
[configuration reference](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/configuration.md#ktor-server-engine); error messages are in
[troubleshooting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md). This page links there instead of repeating them.

Statements about other products (Docker, Kubernetes, cloud load balancers, proxies) were checked against their
documentation on 2026-11-05 and link to it. Products and details this page does not name were not checked: read their
documentation before you rely on them.

### How a client gets to HTTP/3

1. The client connects over TCP and TLS (HTTP/1.1; the TCP side's ALPN is `http/1.1`).
2. The response carries `Alt-Svc: h3=":<port>"; ma=86400` (RFC 7838): HTTP/3 is on UDP, on that port of the same host,
   for 24 hours.
3. The client opens QUIC to that UDP port. The TLS handshake there uses the origin's host name (SNI) and checks the
   same certificate, with ALPN `h3`.
4. The client caches the alternative. If UDP does not get through it falls back to TCP; the Kuicksilver client then
   marks the alternative broken for a while ([Ktor: Racing and fallback](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#racing-and-fallback)).

So the TCP port, the UDP port, the `Alt-Svc` header and the certificate all have to work for HTTP/3. When one of them
is missing, clients quietly stay on HTTP/1.1.

### Ports and Alt-Svc

Every `tlsConnector` serves HTTP/1.1 on TCP and HTTP/3 on UDP **with the same port number** and the same `host`
(default `0.0.0.0`), and so does a plain connector when the configuration has an `identity` (with `EngineMain`, the
`kuicksilver.tls.*` keys). The engine binds both as a pair: a fixed port whose UDP side is taken fails the start
([Ktor: HTTP/3 on the server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http3-on-the-server)). Open, forward and publish **both** `<port>/tcp` and
`<port>/udp` everywhere on the way.

The engine's `Alt-Svc` names the port it bound, `h3=":<bound port>"` (no host: the same host as the request).
That is right only when clients reach the UDP port under the same number. When a NAT, a container port mapping or a
load balancer exposes another number, clients would try the wrong port. Two fixes:

- Map the same number on both sides (`443` outside to `443` inside), so the engine's header is right as it is.
- Or let the application send its own `Alt-Svc`. The engine never replaces an `Alt-Svc` the application set, so the
  application then also follows the run-time switch `engine.http3Advertising` (below) itself. Use it only on
  connectors that do serve HTTP/3: not on a plain connector without TLS, not on one with an `sniSelector`, and not when
  the start logged "HTTP/3 is not served ..." (a UDP bind failure, a platform without a QUIC server, `udpSocketCount`
  above 1 without the accelerated socket); there the header would send clients to a port where nothing answers:

```kotlin
// guide:deployment:public-alt-svc
@file:OptIn(ExperimentalKuicksilverApi::class)   // experimental API (at the top of the file)
val publicPort = 443   // the UDP port clients reach (the load balancer's or the NAT's), not the one bound here
lateinit var engine: KuicksilverApplicationEngine
val server = embeddedServer(Kuicksilver, configure = {
    tlsConnector(identity) { port = 8443 }
}) {
    intercept(ApplicationCallPipeline.Plugins) {
        // an Alt-Svc the application sets is never replaced, so it follows engine.http3Advertising itself
        val h3 = engine.http3Advertising == Http3Advertising.On
        call.response.header("Alt-Svc", if (h3) "h3=\":$publicPort\"; ma=86400" else "clear")
    }
}
engine = server.engine
```

The sample also sends its header on HTTP/3 responses, where the engine sends none under `On`; that only repeats what the
client already uses.

The client side has its own rule: the Kuicksilver client ignores an alternative on an unprivileged port (1024 and up) for
an origin on a privileged one, as Chromium does ([Ktor: Discovery and Alt-Svc](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#discovery-and-alt-svc)).
So for an origin on `https://host/` (port 443), HTTP/3 must also be reachable on a port below 1024, in practice UDP 443.

`ma=86400` means clients remember the alternative for a day. To withdraw HTTP/3, use `Clear` or `Drain` (below), which
send `Alt-Svc: clear`, rather than closing the UDP port, and keep that mode for at least 24 hours: `clear` only reaches
clients that come back over TCP, so a client that cached the alternative and returns within its `ma` still tries QUIC.
Clients that find the UDP port closed wait for their QUIC attempt to time out before they fall back. `altSvc = false` (`kuicksilver.altSvc` with `EngineMain`) stops the
engine's header entirely: then only clients that try HTTP/3 without being told (the Kuicksilver client's `Preferred`
mode or `quicHints`, `curl --http3`) use it.

The engine does not publish DNS HTTPS records (RFC 9460); publishing one in your DNS zone is up to you. A record such as
`example.com. 300 IN HTTPS 1 . alpn=h3,h2` lets clients that look them up (browsers, and the Kuicksilver client with
`http3 { httpsRecords = ... }`, see [HTTPS records](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#https-records-experimental)) use HTTP/3 from the first
request; for a port other than 443 the name is `_<port>._https.<host>`.

### Firewalls and security groups

- Allow inbound **UDP** on the port, next to TCP: in the host firewall (`ufw`, `firewalld`, `nftables`; Windows
  Defender Firewall, see [troubleshooting: Windows](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#windows)) and in the cloud's security group or
  network ACL. A rule for TCP 443 alone is the most common reason a server serves HTTP/1.1 but no client ever arrives over
  QUIC.
- Answers leave from the same UDP port, and from the address the kernel's route picks (the address the client sent to
  only on a host with one address; see [Reply addresses](#reply-addresses)). A stateful firewall allows them once the
  inbound flow is allowed. A stateless
  network ACL needs an outbound rule for UDP from the port to the clients' ports.
- Many corporate and guest networks block UDP 443 on the client side. You cannot fix that from the server. Clients
  fall back to TCP: the Kuicksilver client reports `FallbackReason.HandshakeTimeout` and then `BrokenAlternative`
  ([Ktor: Why did this request not use HTTP/3?](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#why-did-this-request-not-use-http3)).

### Containers

#### Docker

Docker publishes TCP unless a mapping says `/udp`; publish both protocols on the same number
([Docker: port publishing](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/port-publishing/): "`-p 8080:80/udp` Map port `8080` on
the Docker host to UDP port `80` in the container"):

```sh
docker run -p 443:443/tcp -p 443:443/udp my-server-image
```

```dockerfile
EXPOSE 443/tcp 443/udp
```

`EXPOSE` only documents ports; the `-p` mappings publish them. With `-p 8443:443/udp` (another host port) the engine's
`Alt-Svc` names 443, which is wrong outside: map the same number or send your own header ([above](#ports-and-alt-svc)).
On Linux, `--network host` skips Docker's port mapping, and the engine binds the host's ports directly.

The UDP buffer limits are kernel settings of the host ([below](#udp-socket-buffers)). Set them on the host (the
Kubernetes node), not in the image.

#### Kubernetes

A `Service` carries the TCP and the UDP port as two entries with the same number:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-server
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local   # keep the client's address (see below)
  selector:
    app: my-server
  ports:
    - name: https
      protocol: TCP
      port: 443
      targetPort: 443
    - name: h3
      protocol: UDP
      port: 443
      targetPort: 443
```

The pod spec should declare `containerPort: 443` with `protocol: TCP` and another with `protocol: UDP` as well
(`containerPort` is informational: the Service's `targetPort` decides where traffic goes).

- **Mixed protocols in one `LoadBalancer` Service** are stable since Kubernetes 1.26 (the `MixedProtocolLBService` gate
  is removed), but "The set of protocols that can be used for load balanced Services is defined by your cloud provider;
  they may impose restrictions beyond what the Kubernetes API enforces"
  ([Kubernetes: Service, load balancers with mixed protocol types](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#load-balancers-with-mixed-protocol-types)).
  Check that your provider's load balancer controller supports TCP and UDP on one port. Where it does not, use two
  Services (one TCP, one UDP) behind the same address if the provider can share one, or a load balancer you configure
  yourself.
- **The client's address.** With the default `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster`, packets may be source-NATed to a
  node's address. "If you set `service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy` to the value `Local`, kube-proxy only proxies proxy
  requests to local endpoints, and does not forward traffic to other nodes. This approach preserves the original source
  IP address" ([Kubernetes: Using Source IP](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/services/source-ip/)). This matters more
  for QUIC than for TCP. The QUIC endpoint limits connections **per client IP address** (`maxConnectionsPerIp`, 256), and
  that limit cannot be changed from the Ktor engine yet ([Security limits](#security-limits)); the TCP connectors'
  per-address limit, `maxTcpConnectionsPerIp`, is off by default and should stay off behind a source NAT. Behind a source NAT, every
  client counts against the node's address, and so does the stateless answer limit (8 per second per address): Retry
  packets and refusals beyond it are dropped, and those clients see a handshake timeout instead. Address validation
  tokens are also bound to the address the server sees.
- **Rolling updates.** A graceful stop already does what an HTTP/3 client needs ([Ktor: Graceful stop](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#graceful-stop)):
  GOAWAY to every live HTTP/3 connection, and new QUIC clients refused with CONNECTION_REFUSED (under the stateless rate
  limit) instead of timing out. Stop the server with Ktor's `shutdownGracePeriod` and `shutdownTimeout`; the larger of the
  two bounds the stop (keep the timeout ≥ the grace period), so keep the `preStop` delay plus `shutdownTimeout` below
  the pod's `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.
  Clients like the Kuicksilver client recover quickly: it treats `CONNECTION_REFUSED` as transient, and a connection
  the pod closes with H3_NO_ERROR after its GOAWAY (at the end of the grace period) as an orderly end; either way the affected call falls
  back to TCP once (when it may be repeated) and the next one tries HTTP/3 again, which another pod may take. Neither
  marks the alternative broken ([Ktor: Racing and fallback](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#racing-and-fallback); before 0.3.0 both did, for 5
  minutes doubling up to 2 days). Switching a pod to `Http3Advertising.Drain` before it stops has a cost: its responses send
  `Alt-Svc: clear` for the whole origin, not just that pod, so clients that get one drop the alternative until another
  response announces it again. Use `Drain` to take HTTP/3 out of service, not for routine restarts.

### Load balancers and proxies

#### What can sit in front of the server

| In front | HTTP/3 reaches Kuicksilver? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing (public address on the host) | yes | the simplest setup |
| An L4 load balancer that passes UDP through (cloud network load balancer, `kube-proxy`, IPVS, nginx `stream`) | yes | per-flow routing, see [connection IDs](#connection-ids-and-several-instances); with direct server return (IPVS-DR, a VIP on `lo`) bind `host` to the VIP, see [reply addresses](#reply-addresses) |
| An L7 proxy that terminates HTTP/3 itself (CDN, nginx `http`, other reverse proxies) | **no** | the proxy speaks HTTP/3 to clients and HTTP/1.1 (or HTTP/2) to the server; Kuicksilver then serves only that TCP side. Set `altSvc = false` (or strip the header at the proxy): the engine's `h3=":<bound port>"` would otherwise pass through and point clients at that port on the proxy's host |

Notes on specific products (checked 2026-11-05):

- **AWS Network Load Balancer.** Listeners support "TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP\_UDP, QUIC, TCP\_QUIC"; "To support both TCP and
  UDP on the same port, create a TCP\_UDP listener", and its target groups must use TCP\_UDP
  ([AWS: NLB listeners](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html)).
  Client IP preservation "can't be disabled for UDP, TCP\_UDP, QUIC, and TCP\_QUIC target groups"
  ([AWS: NLB target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)),
  so the per-IP limit sees real clients. Use TCP\_UDP with Kuicksilver. The QUIC and TCP\_QUIC listeners route by
  QUIC connection ID: **not verified** with Kuicksilver's QUIC-LB connection IDs (below).
- **Cloudflare** (proxied hostname): HTTP/3 ends at Cloudflare's edge; "HTTP/3 connection to the origin is not yet
  supported" ([Cloudflare: HTTP/3](https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http3/)). Cloudflare then
  reaches a Kuicksilver origin over TCP, and the origin's UDP port only serves clients that reach it directly. Set
  `altSvc = false` on the origin, so its `Alt-Svc` does not reach clients through Cloudflare.
- **nginx** as an L7 proxy terminates HTTP/3 itself and talks to the upstream with `proxy_http_version 1.0 | 1.1 | 2`
  (HTTP/2 since 1.29.4, HTTP/1.1 the default since 1.29.7;
  [nginx: proxy_http_version](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html#proxy_http_version)). A
  Kuicksilver upstream serves HTTP/1.1; set `altSvc = false` on it, or drop the header with `proxy_hide_header Alt-Svc`.
  For UDP passthrough, the `stream` module's `listen ... udp`
  "configures a listening socket for working with datagrams", with `reuseport` "to handle packets from the same address
  and port in the same session"
  ([nginx: stream listen](https://nginx.org/en/docs/stream/ngx_stream_core_module.html#listen)). By default nginx connects
  to the upstream from its own address, so every client shares nginx's address against the per-IP limit.
- **Google Cloud (GKE) and Azure:** whether their load balancers take TCP and UDP on one port in one Service was **not
  verified** for this page; see their documentation.
- **HAProxy, Envoy, Caddy, other CDNs:** **not verified**. The table above still applies: find out whether the product
  passes QUIC through at layer 4 or terminates HTTP/3.

#### Reply addresses

A client drops QUIC packets from an address it did not send to (RFC 9000 section 9), so every answer must leave from the
address the client used. With the default `host = "0.0.0.0"` (or `::`) the engine's accelerated UDP socket (Linux,
Android, macOS, iOS, Windows; 0.3.0) learns the destination of every datagram (`IP_PKTINFO` / `IPV6_PKTINFO`) and
sends that connection's packets, and any stateless answer to it, from that address. This covers a host with several
addresses, a secondary IP, a floating or virtual IP (keepalived) and a VIP on `lo` for IPVS direct routing or similar
direct server return. A connection keeps the server address its client first reached: packets of the same client that
later arrive at another of the server's addresses are processed, and the answers still leave from the first one (only a
client migrates, and it does so by changing its own address).

Before 0.3.0, and still with the portable socket (`IoPreference.Portable`, the JVM without the native library, a
Kotlin/Native target without `ksl_udp`; the log says "using the portable socket" when it falls back), the kernel picks
the source from the route to the client: on such hosts the answers leave from the wrong address and QUIC never
connects while TCP works. There, bind the connector's `host` to the address clients send to (one connector per address
when there are several).

#### Connection IDs and several instances

A QUIC connection is identified by connection IDs, not by the 4-tuple, so it survives a client's change of address (NAT
rebinding, Wi-Fi to cellular; [QUIC: Migration and paths](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#migration-and-paths)). An L4 load balancer that hashes
the 4-tuple does not know this:

- While the client's address and port stay the same, all its packets reach the same instance, and everything works.
- When they change, the packets may hash to another instance. That instance has no state for the connection and
  cannot end it either: Stateless Reset tokens come from a key of the endpoint that issued the connection
  ([QUIC: Stateless reset](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#stateless-reset)). The connection then stalls until the client's idle timeout and
  the client reconnects. With a single instance behind the load balancer this cannot happen.
- Retry tokens and NEW_TOKEN address tokens are sealed with keys of one server process. A Retry token is valid for
  10 s and bound to the client's address and port; one that another instance issued does not open, so the attempt is
  refused with a stateless CONNECTION_CLOSE carrying INVALID_TOKEN (RFC 9000 section 8.1.3) and that connection attempt
  fails. Under per-flow routing the Initial after a Retry comes from the same 4-tuple and reaches the same instance, so
  this happens only when the flow moves within those seconds. A NEW_TOKEN token from another instance counts as no
  token ([QUIC: Admission and endpoint limits](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#admission-and-endpoint-limits)): the client may be asked for a
  Retry again, at the cost of a round trip.

QUIC-LB (draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers-21) lets a load balancer route by a server ID encoded in the connection ID. Since
0.3.0 the engine offers it, experimentally: `quicLoadBalancer = QuicLbConfig(...)` with the values your load balancer's
configuration agent assigned each instance, and `engine.updateLoadBalancer(next)` to roll out a new configuration
([QUIC: Behind a load balancer](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#behind-a-load-balancer)). Without a QUIC-LB load balancer, put one instance behind
each address, or accept that a client that changes address while connected to a multi-instance pool reconnects. The engine does not offer a QUIC
preferred address (`QuicServerConfig.preferredAddress`, [QUIC: Migration and paths](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#migration-and-paths)) either;
that needs the QUIC API directly.

### The host

#### UDP socket buffers

A QUIC server receives everything through one UDP socket per loop. A burst that does not fit into the socket's receive
buffer is dropped by the kernel, and QUIC sees it as loss. Kuicksilver asks for large buffers itself; the OS caps what
it gets:

| Platform (socket) | What Kuicksilver asks for | What limits it |
|---|---|---|
| Linux, Android (accelerated `ksl` socket) | `SO_RCVBUF` and `SO_SNDBUF` of 7 MiB | `net.core.rmem_max` and `net.core.wmem_max`: Linux silently caps a larger request to them (`socket(7)`). The default is distribution-dependent and often about 208 KiB |
| macOS, iOS (accelerated `ksl` socket) | 7 MiB, halved until the kernel accepts it (the last try is 448 KiB; after that the OS default stays) | `kern.ipc.maxsockbuf` (on macOS 8 MiB by default, less overhead; iOS not checked) |
| Windows (accelerated `ksl` socket) | 7 MiB, once | Windows' own limits |
| JVM portable socket (when `ksl` is not used) | 8 MiB | the same OS limits |

Kuicksilver does not read the size back, does not log it, and does not use `SO_RCVBUFFORCE`. The engine has no option
for it ("UDP socket buffer sizes are not configurable yet", [Ktor: HTTP/3 on the server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http3-on-the-server)).
On Linux, raise the limits so the request is granted in full (values in bytes; 8 MiB, 8 388 608, covers the 7 MiB of
the `ksl` socket and the 8 MiB of the JVM portable socket):

```sh
sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.wmem_max          # what the host allows now
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=8388608 net.core.wmem_max=8388608
# keep it across reboots
printf 'net.core.rmem_max=8388608\nnet.core.wmem_max=8388608\n' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/90-quic.conf
```

Signs that the buffer is too small: receive errors growing under load (`netstat -su`, "receive buffer errors", or
`RcvbufErrors` in `/proc/net/snmp`) and losses in a qlog trace that the network does not explain. These counters are
per network namespace: for a server in a container, read them inside it (or with `nsenter -t <pid> -n`).

#### GSO, GRO and several loops

On Linux and Android the accelerated socket sends runs of equal-sized datagrams with one `sendmsg` and `UDP_SEGMENT`
(GSO), and receives coalesced datagrams with `UDP_GRO`. It probes both when the socket opens, and turns GSO off by itself
if the kernel or the driver fails a send with it. Darwin has neither (one datagram per call). Windows uses USO and URO
where the system grants them. Nothing needs to be set, but older kernels lack the options: UDP GSO arrived in Linux 4.18
and UDP GRO in 5.0. The engine does not log whether they were granted; `DatagramIo.open(...).capabilities`
(`gsoMaxSegments`, `gro`) shows it for a socket you open yourself on the same host
([QUIC: Binding an endpoint and connecting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#binding-an-endpoint-and-connecting)).

`udpSocketCount` (`kuicksilver.udpSocketCount`, default 1) runs that many endpoint loops on the port. On Linux and
Android each has its own socket on `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the kernel spreads client flows over them; a connection whose
packets the kernel hashes onto another loop's socket (after a NAT rebinding) is forwarded inside the process. On macOS,
iOS and Windows the loops share one socket, whose receiver hands each datagram to the loop its connection ID names, so a
rebound client needs no forwarding at all. Either way several loops have none of the load balancer problems above, and
one connection is no faster with more loops ([QUIC: Several loops on one port](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#several-loops-on-one-port)).
Only a JVM that fell back to the portable socket cannot run more than one: there the start does not fail, the engine
logs "HTTP/3 is not served on port <port>: ..." and serves HTTP/1.1 alone, without `Alt-Svc`
([troubleshooting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#unsupportedoperationexception-for-loops--1)).

If the accelerated socket cannot open, the JVM falls back to a portable socket without these features, with a warning
in the log; a Kotlin/Native server then serves HTTP/1.1 only
([troubleshooting: The accelerated socket is not used](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#the-accelerated-socket-is-not-used)).

#### MTU

QUIC starts at 1200-byte packets and raises them with DPLPMTUD. Tunnels with a small MTU (VPNs, some overlay networks)
are covered by black-hole detection ([QUIC: Path MTU](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#path-mtu),
[troubleshooting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#transfers-stall-over-a-vpn-or-tunnel-mtu-black-hole)).

### Certificates

- One identity serves both sides: the same chain and key over TCP and over QUIC. The certificate must cover the host
  name clients use for the origin. The alternative in `Alt-Svc` has no host of its own, so the name is the same.
- A `tlsConnector` with an `sniSelector` serves no HTTP/3 (warning at start): QUIC cannot pick an identity per SNI name
  yet. Give each name its own connector, or use one certificate for all names.
- Renewed certificates can be put in place without a restart: a `TlsIdentity.Reloadable` and `reload(...)`, or with
  `EngineMain` the key `kuicksilver.tls.reloadInterval` that watches the PEM files of `kuicksilver.tls.certificateChain` and
  `kuicksilver.tls.privateKey` ([Ktor: Certificate rotation](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#certificate-rotation),
  [TLS: Rotating the server certificate](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#rotating-the-server-certificate)). New handshakes on TCP and QUIC take the
  new certificate; open connections keep theirs.

### Turning HTTP/3 off without a restart

On the server, `engine.http3Advertising` (experimental) is read per response and per new QUIC client
([Ktor: Turning HTTP/3 off on the server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#turning-http3-off-on-the-server)):

| Value | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `On` | normal operation |
| `Clear` | HTTP/3 should stop being offered, but connections that use it may finish in their own time |
| `Drain` | HTTP/3 must go now: GOAWAY to live connections, new QUIC clients refused with CONNECTION_REFUSED (within the stateless rate limit; beyond it they time out), so they fall back at once; a Kuicksilver client does not mark the alternative broken for the refusal and is back on HTTP/3 as soon as the server announces it again |

The UDP socket stays bound in every mode. To block UDP for good, use the firewall, after at least 24 hours (`ma=86400`)
in `Drain` or `Clear`, so that returning clients have dropped the cached alternative first; clients that do not come
back within that time have let it expire. The value is per engine and starts at `On`. Behind a load balancer,
set it on every instance.

On the client, an application can switch HTTP/3 off from its remote configuration with `http3 { http3Allowed }` and take
open connections out of use with `client.closeHttp3Connections()`
([Ktor: Turning HTTP/3 off remotely](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#turning-http3-off-remotely)).

### Security limits

The HTTP/3 listener runs the QUIC endpoint's protections ([QUIC: Admission and endpoint limits](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#admission-and-endpoint-limits),
[threat model 3.1](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/spec/threat-model.md#31-amplification) and [3.2](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/spec/threat-model.md#32-resource-exhaustion)):

- **Amplification.** Before a client's address is validated, the server sends at most three times what it received
  (RFC 9000 section 8.1).
- **Retry.** `quicAdmission` (a `ConnectionAdmission`) decides per new client. The default asks unvalidated clients for a
  Retry under handshake load; `ConnectionAdmission.AlwaysRetry` always does. Clients that bring a valid address token skip
  it.
- **Hard limits.** `maxConnections` 10 000, `maxConnectionsPerIp` 256 and `acceptQueue` 128 per listener, and stateless
  answers (Retry, refusals, Version Negotiation, Stateless Reset) rate-limited to 8 per second per address and 1000 in
  total; what goes beyond is dropped, and such clients see a handshake timeout. The engine does not let you change these
  yet ([configuration](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/configuration.md#ktor-server-engine)). This is why a source NAT in front of the server matters
  ([Kubernetes](#kubernetes)): every client behind it shares both limits.
- **TCP connection limits.** `maxTcpConnections` (10 000 per connector: at the limit the connector stops accepting and
  the OS backlog holds new clients; keep it below `ulimit -n`) and `maxTcpConnectionsPerIp` (off by default: behind a
  proxy, load balancer, SNAT or NAT every client shares one address; enable it, e.g. 256, only when the server faces
  clients directly; one more from that address is reset at accept, which a proxy reports as 502/503), HTTP/1.1 and
  HTTP/2 alike ([Connection limits](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#connection-limits)).
- **Transport and HTTP/3 settings.** `quic` (a `QuicConfig`: idle timeout, windows, congestion control), `http3Settings`,
  and on TCP `requestHeaderTimeoutSeconds` and `connectionIdleTimeoutSeconds` against slow clients
  ([Ktor: Server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#server)).

### Observability

- The application's log gets the engine's own messages, such as "HTTP/3 is not served on port ...". The `logger`
  (warnings on standard error by default) gets the QUIC endpoints' diagnostics, such as the fallback to the portable
  socket; `logger = KuicksilverLogger.stderr(LogLevel.Debug)` adds each QUIC connection's lifecycle.
- `eventListener` (`KuicksilverServerEventListener`) hears connections per protocol (`connectionOpened` with
  `HTTP/3.0`), failed TLS handshakes and requests, which you can count; `connectionListener` hears every QUIC connection with its close reason.
- `qlog = AsyncQlogSink(DirectoryQlogSink(dir), sampleEvery = 100)` writes a trace per sampled connection, for
  [qvis](https://qvis.quictools.info/).

See [Ktor: Observability](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#observability-experimental) for a sample. The engine does not expose the endpoint's
`EndpointStats` counters (refusals, datagrams received). On the server, "does any QUIC arrive at all?" is answered by
`connectionListener`, a debug log, or a packet capture.

### Checking a deployment

From a machine outside your network:

```sh
# 1. TCP side: the Alt-Svc header (h3 with the public port; "clear" under Clear or Drain)
curl -sI https://example.com/ | grep -i '^alt-svc'

# 2. UDP side: HTTP/3 only, no fallback (needs a curl built with HTTP/3: `curl -V` lists HTTP3)
curl --http3-only -sI https://example.com/

# 3. On the server: does UDP arrive at all?
sudo tcpdump -ni any udp port 443
```

`curl --http3-only` tries QUIC on the URL's port. When `Alt-Svc` advertises another port, test that one
(`https://example.com:<advertised port>/`). Run `tcpdump` on the port the engine bound; for a container, inside its
network namespace (`nsenter -t <pid> -n tcpdump ...`) or on the host's published port.

`curl --http3-only` fails when QUIC does not get through, so it tells a blocked UDP path apart from a client that just
chose TCP ([curl: HTTP/3](https://curl.se/docs/http3.html)).

From a Kuicksilver client, every response says how it was served and, if not over HTTP/3, why:
`response.kuicksilverDiagnostics?.fallback`, or one log line per call with `engine { logger = KuicksilverLogger.stderr(LogLevel.Info) }`
([Ktor: Why did this request not use HTTP/3?](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#why-did-this-request-not-use-http3)). Keep in mind that in `Auto`
mode the first call to an origin goes over HTTP/1.1 (`NoAlternative`) unless a `FileAltSvcStore` remembers the
alternative from an earlier run; HTTP/3 starts from the next call.

### Troubleshooting checklist

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| No `Alt-Svc` in responses | the server log ("HTTP/3 is not served ...": the UDP bind, no QUIC server on the platform, `udpSocketCount` above 1 without the accelerated socket); `http3` and `altSvc` on; an `sniSelector` on the connector; a proxy in front that strips the header ([troubleshooting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#the-server-serves-http11-but-no-http3)) |
| `Alt-Svc: clear` | `engine.http3Advertising` is `Clear` or `Drain` |
| `Alt-Svc` names the wrong port | a port mapping or load balancer with another number: map the same number or send your own header ([Ports and Alt-Svc](#ports-and-alt-svc)) |
| `curl --http3-only` times out, `tcpdump` shows nothing | UDP is blocked before the server: firewall, security group, `-p .../udp` missing, the Service has no UDP port, the load balancer has no UDP listener |
| `tcpdump` shows Initials, no answer | the host firewall drops them; the per-IP or stateless rate limit or the admission policy drops them (all clients behind one NAT address); answers leave from another source address ([reply addresses](#reply-addresses)) |
| `curl --http3-only` fails with a TLS error | the certificate does not cover the name, or a connector with `sniSelector` (no HTTP/3) |
| Client `fallback = HandshakeTimeout`, then `BrokenAlternative` | UDP blocked on the client's network or in front of the server |
| Client `fallback = Refused` | the server is in `Drain`, stopping, or its accept queue is full (`h3Failure` code 0x2, CONNECTION_REFUSED: transient, the next call tries HTTP/3 again); another code: the server's QUIC listener |
| Client `fallback = TlsFailure` | the certificate on the UDP side, its `h3` ALPN |
| Client `fallback = NoAlternative` on every call | the client never saw `Alt-Svc` (a proxy strips it), or the alternative's port is unprivileged for a privileged origin |
| Connections drop when clients change networks | an L4 load balancer with several instances ([Connection IDs](#connection-ids-and-several-instances)) |
| Throughput low, loss under load | UDP buffer limits ([UDP socket buffers](#udp-socket-buffers)), GSO missing on an old kernel |

## Configuration reference

Every option of Kuicksilver in one place: its type, its default as the code sets it, the range the builder
accepts and what it does. The guides explain how the options work together; each section links its guide. Options
marked *experimental* need `@OptIn(ExperimentalKuicksilverApi::class)`, *delicate* ones
`@OptIn(DelicateKuicksilverApi::class)` ([stability](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/stability.md)).

All configuration objects are immutable and validated when built: a builder's `build()` (or the DSL function around
it) throws `IllegalArgumentException` naming the first value out of range, or `TlsException.Config` for a TLS setting.
Problems that only show at run time are in [troubleshooting](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md). The *Since* column names the release
that introduced the option (`0.3.0`: the release in preparation); `tools/check/config-table.sh` checks every public
option of the configuration classes against these tables, defaults and releases included.

Contents: [where options are set](#where-each-option-is-set) · [QUIC transport](#quicconfig) · [QUIC client and server](#quicclientconfig-and-quicserverconfig) ·
[QUIC endpoint](#quicendpointconfig) · [other QUIC options](#other-quic-options) · [TLS](#tlsconfig) ·
[trust](#trustconfig) · [identities and key logging](#identities-and-key-logging) · [HTTP/3](#http3settings) · [HTTP/2](#http2settings) ·
[Ktor client](#ktor-client-engine) · [Ktor server](#ktor-server-engine) · [system properties and environment
variables](#system-properties-and-environment-variables) · [fixed limits](#fixed-limits)

### Where each option is set

| Object | Kotlin API | Ktor client | Ktor server | `EngineMain` key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`QuicConfig`](#quicconfig) | `quicConfig { }` | `engine { quic = … }` | `quic = …` (`quicMaxIdleTimeout`) | |
| [`QuicEndpointConfig`](#quicendpointconfig) | `quicEndpointConfig { }` | `engine { http3 { endpoint = … } }` | only `quicAdmission`, `quicLoadBalancer`, `logger`, `qlog`, `connectionListener` and `udpSocketCount` (`loops`) reach it; the other limits keep their defaults | `kuicksilver.udpSocketCount` |
| [`TlsConfig`](#tlsconfig) | `tlsConfig(role) { }` | `engine { trust = …; identity = …; tls { } }` | `tlsConnector(identity) { }` | `kuicksilver.tls.*` |
| [`Http3Settings`](#http3settings) | `http3Settings { }` | `engine { http3 { settings = … } }` | `http3Settings = …` | `kuicksilver.http3` (on/off) |
| [`Http2Settings`](#http2settings) | `Http2Settings(…)` | `engine { http2 { settings = … } }` | `http2Settings = …` | `kuicksilver.http2` (on/off) |
| [client engine](#ktor-client-engine) | | `HttpClient(Kuicksilver) { engine { … } }` | | |
| [server engine](#ktor-server-engine) | | | `embeddedServer(Kuicksilver) { … }` | `kuicksilver.*`, `ktor.deployment.*` |

### QuicConfig

Transport settings of a connection: `quicConfig { }` (`QuicConfig.Builder`), `QuicConfig.Default` for all defaults,
`toBuilder()` (*experimental*) to change one value of an existing config. Guide: [QUIC](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#configuration).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxIdleTimeout` | `Duration` | 30 s | zero or positive and finite | 0.2.0 | our `max_idle_timeout`; the connection closes silently after the smaller of both peers' values (never below 3 x PTO) without traffic, with `ConnectionLost.Timeout(TimeoutKind.Idle)`. `Duration.ZERO` advertises none and leaves the timeout to the peer |
| `handshakeTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | positive (`Duration.INFINITE` leaves only the idle timeout) | 0.2.0 | a connection whose handshake has not completed by then closes with `TimeoutKind.Handshake` |
| `keepAlive` | `Duration?` | `null` (off) | positive and finite; at most 3/4 of `maxIdleTimeout` unless that is `ZERO` | 0.2.0 | PING interval while the application is quiet; PINGs go out at least every half of the effective idle timeout, so a peer with a shorter timeout does not close the connection (as quic-go). With `maxIdleTimeout = ZERO` it holds the connection against the peer's timeout |
| `initialStreamWindow` | `Long` (bytes) | 524 288 (512 KiB) | 1..`maxStreamWindow` | 0.2.0 | receive window of each stream at its start (`initial_max_stream_data_*`); doubles while the application reads a whole window in under four RTTs |
| `initialConnectionWindow` | `Long` (bytes) | 786 432 (768 KiB) | 1..`maxConnectionWindow` | 0.2.0 | receive window of the connection at its start (`initial_max_data`); kept at least 1.5 x the largest stream window |
| `maxStreamWindow` | `Long` (bytes) | 6 291 456 (6 MiB) | at least `initialStreamWindow` | 0.2.0 | ceiling of a stream's receive window: the most unread data one stream holds |
| `maxConnectionWindow` | `Long` (bytes) | 15 728 640 (15 MiB) | at least `initialConnectionWindow` | 0.2.0 | ceiling of the connection's receive window |
| `maxBidiStreams` | `Long` | 100 | 0..2^60 | 0.2.0 | bidirectional streams the peer may have open at once (`initial_max_streams_bidi`); raised by MAX_STREAMS as streams close. A stream counts as closed once the application took it from `acceptStream()` and consumed it (read to the end or saw its reset), so a peer cannot open more streams than this while the application accepts none |
| `maxUniStreams` | `Long` | 100 | 0..2^60 | 0.2.0 | the same for unidirectional streams; HTTP/3 needs at least 3 (RFC 9114 §6.2): `Http3Endpoint` and the Ktor engines with HTTP/3 refuse less |
| `maxSendBuffer` | `Long` (bytes) | 4 194 304 (4 MiB) | 1..2^62 | 0.2.0 | unacknowledged send data the connection buffers over all streams; writers wait beyond it |
| `maxAckDelay` | `Duration` | 25 ms | below 2^14 ms | 0.2.0 | our `max_ack_delay` |
| `ackDelayExponent` | `Int` | 3 | 0..20 | 0.2.0 | our `ack_delay_exponent` |
| `activeConnectionIdLimit` | `Int` | 4 | at least 2 | 0.2.0 | our `active_connection_id_limit`: connection IDs of the peer kept for migration and rotation |
| `connectionIdLength` | `Int` (bytes) | 8 | 4..20; must equal `QuicEndpointConfig.connectionIdLength` | 0.2.0 | length of the connection IDs we issue |
| `maxUdpPayloadSize` | `Int` (bytes) | 1452 | 1200..65 527; a `QuicEndpoint` refuses more than 1500 at `bind`/`connect` | 0.2.0 | advertised `max_udp_payload_size` and the upper bound of PMTUD ([Path MTU](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#path-mtu)) |
| `versions` | `List<VersionProfile>` | `listOf(VersionProfile.V1)` | non-empty, no duplicates | 0.2.0 | versions in preference order; `listOf(V2, V1)` opts into QUIC v2 (RFC 9368/9369) |
| `initialVersion` | `VersionProfile?` | `null` (first of `versions`) | one of `versions` | 0.2.0 | the version of a client's first flight |
| `initialRtt` | `Duration` | 333 ms | (0, 10 s] | 0.2.0 | RTT assumed before the first sample: the first PTO is 3 x this (1 s, 2 s, 4 s at the default) and a path validation lasts at least 6 x this. A client endpoint replaces it with the last smoothed RTT to the same server address (see [fixed limits](#fixed-limits)) |
| `defaultStreamErrorCode` | `Long` | 0 | 0..2^62-1 | 0.2.0 | code of the STOP_SENDING / RESET_STREAM sent when a stream channel is cancelled, or when a peer stream is given up before the application accepted it (its `acceptStream()` caller cancelled). An HTTP/3 server (`Http3Endpoint`, the Ktor engine) left at 0, which is no HTTP/3 code, uses H3_REQUEST_REJECTED (0x10b, RFC 9114 §4.1.1: not processed, safe to retry); a code set explicitly is kept |
| `qlog` | `QlogSink?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | a qlog trace per connection ([qlog](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#qlog)); a failing sink stops tracing for that connection only |
| `congestionController` | `() -> CongestionController` | `{ Cubic() }` | return a fresh instance per call | 0.2.0 | controller of each path: `Cubic` (CUBIC with HyStart++), `NewReno`, `Bbr` (*experimental*) ([Congestion control](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#congestion-control)) |
| `greaseQuicBit` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | send the fixed bit randomly when the peer allows it (RFC 9287) |
| `glitchProtection` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | close a connection whose peer keeps making us do useless work ([Glitch protection](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#glitch-protection)) |
| `allowMigration` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | server: follow a client to a new address; `false` advertises `disable_active_migration` and drops datagrams from other addresses |
| `allowMigrationToLoopback` | `Boolean` | `false` |  | 0.2.0 | server: accept a move to a loopback or link-local address from a connection that did not start on one |
| `pmtud` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | DPLPMTUD (RFC 8899) on sockets that set DF; `false` keeps 1200 bytes |
| `followPreferredAddress` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.3.0 | client: move to the server's preferred address after the handshake, once the path there is validated ([Migration and paths](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#migration-and-paths)) |
| `pmtudIcmpHints` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.3.0 | validated ICMP Packet Too Big (Linux, Android) and EMSGSIZE speed up DPLPMTUD as hints, never lowering the MTU without lost probes ([Path MTU](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#path-mtu)) |
| `maxDatagramFrameSize` | `Long` | 65 535 | 0..65 535 | 0.2.0 | our `max_datagram_frame_size` (RFC 9221); 0 turns datagrams off |
| `resetStreamAt` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `false` |  | 0.3.0 | advertise `reset_stream_at`: `QuicStream.resetAt` keeps a stream's first bytes when the peer advertised it too ([quic.md](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#reliable-stream-reset-experimental)) |
| `datagramReceiveQueue` | `Int` | 128 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | received datagrams held for the application; a full queue drops the oldest |
| `datagramSendQueue` | `Int` | 32 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | datagrams queued for sending ([Datagrams](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#datagrams-rfc-9221)) |
| `datagramSendQueueBytes` | `Long` | 1 048 576 (1 MiB) | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | byte ceiling of the same queue |

### QuicClientConfig and QuicServerConfig

`quicClientConfig(tls) { }` and `quicServerConfig(tls) { }` pair a `TlsConfig` with a `QuicConfig`. `build()` throws
`IllegalArgumentException` for a `TlsConfig` of the wrong role ("client config needs a client TlsConfig") and
`TlsException.Config` for one QUIC cannot use: TLS 1.2 allowed, an empty `alpn`, `TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256`, or an
`sniSelector`.

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tls` (constructor) | `TlsConfig` |  | client or server role | 0.3.0 | name to verify, trust, ALPN; identity on a server |
| `quic` | `QuicConfig` | `QuicConfig.Default` | on a server, its `connectionIdLength` must equal the endpoint's | 0.2.0 | transport settings |
| client `earlyData` (*experimental*) | `EarlyDataState` | `Disabled` | `Disabled`, `Allowed`, `Required` | 0.2.0 | keep the server's session tickets (per endpoint, single use) and send 0-RTT through `QuicEndpoint.connectEarly`; `Required` fails the connection with `ZeroRttRejected` when 0-RTT is refused or impossible ([0-RTT](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#0-rtt-opt-in-experimental)) |
| server `earlyData` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `false` | not with client certificates | 0.2.0 | accept 0-RTT: fresh tickets only (±10 s ticket age), once per ticket, only for the configuration that issued it |
| server `earlyDataContext` (*experimental*) | `ByteArray?` | `null` | at most 256 bytes | 0.2.0 | application settings bound into tickets (`Http3Endpoint` puts its SETTINGS here) |
| client `tokenStore` (*experimental*) | `QuicTokenStore?` | `null` |  | 0.3.0 | keep the servers' NEW_TOKEN tokens and present one on the next connection to the same server name and port: no Retry round trip; links those connections ([Address tokens](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#address-tokens-new_token)) |
| server `preferredAddress` (*experimental*) | `PreferredAddress?` | `null` | IP literals, ports 1..65535, not unspecified or multicast | 0.3.0 | also listen on these addresses (one per family) and offer them in `preferred_address`; clients that follow move there after validating the path ([Migration and paths](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#migration-and-paths)) |
| server `newTokenReplayCapacity` (*experimental*) | `Int` | `1_048_576` | 1..16,777,216 | 0.3.0 | NEW_TOKEN tokens the replay register holds per lifetime (32 bytes each, 32 MiB at the default, allocated on the first token shown); once full a returning client's token counts as absent |
| server `newTokenLifetime` (*experimental*) | `Duration?` | 24 hours | positive, at most 7 days; `null` issues none | 0.3.0 | how long the NEW_TOKEN tokens this server issues validate a returning client's address ([Admission and endpoint limits](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#admission-and-endpoint-limits)) |

### QuicEndpointConfig

The endpoint that owns a socket and its connections: `quicEndpointConfig { }`, `QuicEndpointConfig.Default` (a
client-only endpoint), `toBuilder()` (*experimental*). Guide: [Admission and endpoint limits](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#admission-and-endpoint-limits).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | `QuicServerConfig?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | the server side; `null` is a client-only endpoint, which admits no connection |
| `crypto` | `QuicCrypto` | `KslQuicCrypto` |  | 0.2.0 | TLS and packet protection (OpenSSL through `ksl`) |
| `maxConnections` | `Int` | 10 000 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | beyond this many connections new Initials are dropped silently |
| `acceptQueue` | `Int` | 128 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | handshaken connections waiting for `accept()`, over all loops; while full, a new client is refused statelessly with CONNECTION_REFUSED (0x02). Handshakes in flight do not count |
| `dispatcher` | `CoroutineDispatcher?` | `null` (`Dispatchers.Default.limitedParallelism(1)`) | must stay `null` with `loops > 1` | 0.2.0 | the single-threaded dispatcher of the endpoint loop. While datagrams keep coming the loop reads the ones already queued on this thread; only on its own dispatcher (`null`) does it also wait there up to 1 ms for the next ones (not on Windows), so a dispatcher set here, shared with a UI or a second endpoint, is never held in a socket wait |
| `io` | `(suspend (InetSocketAddress) -> DatagramIo)?` | `null` (`DatagramIo.open` with `IoPreference.Accelerated`) |  | 0.2.0 | how the loop opens its socket; `MemoryNetwork.open` runs the endpoint in memory ([Testing](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#testing-your-application)) |
| `connectionIdLength` | `Int` (bytes) | 8 | 4..20; must equal the `QuicConfig.connectionIdLength` of the server and of every client connection | 0.2.0 | length used to parse short headers |
| `admission` | `ConnectionAdmission` | `ConnectionAdmission.default()` |  | 0.2.0 | decides per new client Initial: `Allow`, `Retry`, `Drop` or `Close(code)`. `default(maxInflightHandshakes = 256, maxHandshakeBufferBytes = 8 MiB)` asks an unvalidated client for a Retry above either and lets in one a Retry or NEW_TOKEN token validated; `ConnectionAdmission.AlwaysRetry` validates every address first |
| `initialQueueCap` | `Int` | 1024 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | new Initials queued for admission per receive batch; more are dropped |
| `maxConnectionsPerIp` | `Int?` | 256 | positive or `null` (no limit) | 0.2.0 | connections one client IP may hold, ports ignored; the excess is dropped silently |
| `maxConnectionLifetime` | `Duration?` | `null` (none) | positive or `null` | 0.2.0 | server connections older than this close with NO_ERROR ("connection lifetime reached") |
| `rejectInitialFromReflectivePorts` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | drop Initials from source ports 53, 123, 1900, 5353 and 11211 (reflection attacks) |
| `statelessPerAddressPerSecond` | `Int` | 8 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | stateless answers (Retry, Version Negotiation, Stateless Reset, refusals) per client address per second |
| `statelessTotalPerSecond` | `Int` | 1000 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | stateless answers per second over all addresses |
| `loops` | `Int` | 1 | 1..255; more than 1 needs a `server` and no `dispatcher` | 0.2.0 | endpoint loops sharing the port: a socket each with `SO_REUSEPORT` on Linux and Android, one socket routed in process elsewhere (every platform since 0.3.0; [Several loops on one port](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#several-loops-on-one-port)) |
| `logger` (*experimental*) | `KuicksilverLogger` | `KuicksilverLogger.Stderr` (warnings and errors on standard error) |  | 0.2.0 | the endpoint's diagnostics; `KuicksilverLogger.None`, `KuicksilverLogger.stderr(LogLevel.Debug)` or your own ([Observability](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#observability)) |
| `listener` (*experimental*) | `ConnectionListener?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | lifecycle callbacks of every connection, on the loop |
| `loadBalancer` (*experimental*) | `QuicLbConfig?` | `null` | needs a `server`, `connectionIdLength` = 1 + server ID + nonce and at least 8, a key next to a `preferredAddress` | 0.3.0 | QUIC-LB server connection IDs (draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers-21); change with `QuicEndpoint.updateLoadBalancer` ([Behind a load balancer](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#behind-a-load-balancer)) |

### Other QUIC options

| Where | Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QuicConnection.openBidi`, `openUni` | `priority: StreamPriority` | `StreamPriority.Default` (`urgency = 3`, `incremental = false`; urgency 0..7) | send order between streams (RFC 9218 levels) |
| `QuicConnection.sendDatagram`, `trySendDatagram` | `policy: DatagramPolicy` | `DropOldest` | `DropOldest`, `LatestWins(key)` or `Reject` when the send queue is full |
| `DatagramIo.open(local, prefer)` | `prefer: IoPreference` | `Accelerated` | `Accelerated`: the `ksl` socket where it exists, `Portable`: NIO on the JVM, `ktor-network` on Kotlin/Native |
| `Cubic(maxDatagramSize, hystart)`, `NewReno(maxDatagramSize)` | | 1200, `true` | the stable congestion controllers |
| `Bbr(maxDatagramSize, random)` (*experimental*) | | 1200, `null` (jitter from send and ACK times) | BBRv3 ([Choosing a congestion controller](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#choosing-a-congestion-controller)) |
| `DirectoryQlogSink(directory)`, `DirectoryQlogSink(directory, maxOpenTraces, maxTotalBytes)` (*experimental*) | | 256 open traces, 1 GiB in all | one `<odcid>_<client\|server>_<random>.sqlog` file per connection, created exclusively, never through a link; creates the directory owner-only and refuses one another user could change |
| `AsyncQlogSink(delegate, queueCapacity, sampleEvery, dispatcher)` (*experimental*) | | 8192 records, 1 (every connection), `Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(1)` | runs a sink off the endpoint loop; a full queue drops records (`dropped`) |
| `NetworkMigrator(connection, networks, openIo, scope)` (*experimental*) | | no defaults; client connections only | follows a `Flow` of networks ([Network changes](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#network-changes)) |
| `QuicConnection.rebind(local, prefer)` (*experimental*) | | `null` (wildcard of the peer's family), `Accelerated` | moves the connection to a fresh socket |
| `followDefaultNetwork(connectivity, scope, local, prefer)` (Android), `followDefaultNetwork(scope, local, prefer)` (Apple) (*experimental*) | | `null`, `Accelerated` | a started `NetworkMigrator` on the default network |
| `QuicEndpoint.shutdown(grace, code, reason)` (*experimental*) | | `code = 0`, `reason = "shutdown"` | graceful shutdown ([Graceful shutdown](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/quic.md#graceful-shutdown)) |

### TlsConfig

`tlsConfig(TlsRole.Client / TlsRole.Server) { }` (`TlsConfig.Builder`); errors are `TlsException.Config`. One
`TlsConfig` drives QUIC, TLS over TCP and `Socket.tls()`. Guide: [TLS](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#configuration).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alpn` | `List<String>` | empty | each name 1..255 UTF-8 bytes, the list at most 255 bytes on the wire; QUIC needs at least one | 0.2.0 | ALPN protocol IDs in preference order |
| `serverName` | `String?` | `null` | a client needs it (or `TrustConfig.ExpectedName`) | 0.2.0 | SNI and the name the certificate must match; an IP literal is verified but never sent as SNI. Servers ignore it |
| `versions` | `TlsVersions` | `Tls13` | QUIC: `Tls13` only | 0.2.0 | TLS 1.3 is the default (RFC 9852); `Tls12And13` allows TLS 1.2 over TCP under the RFC 9325 profile as narrowed by RFC 10015 (ECDHE and AEAD only) |
| `cipherSuites` | `CipherSuites` | `CipherSuites.Default` (AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) | at least one; QUIC refuses `TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256` | 0.2.0 | TLS 1.3 suites in preference order |
| `identity` | `TlsIdentity?` | `null` | a server needs an identity or an `sniSelector` | 0.2.0 | certificate chain and key; `TlsIdentity.reloadable(...)` for one replaced at run time ([TLS guide](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#rotating-the-server-certificate)) |
| `trust` | `TrustConfig` | `TrustConfig.Platform` | with `clientAuth` other than `None`: `AnchoredCa`, optionally under `Pinned` | 0.2.0 | how the peer is verified ([below](#trustconfig)) |
| `clientAuth` | `ClientAuth` | `None` | servers only | 0.2.0 | `None`, `Optional` or `Required` client certificates |
| `sniSelector` | `(suspend (ClientHelloInfo) -> ServerTlsOverride?)?` | `null` | servers, TCP only (QUIC refuses it) | 0.2.0 | picks a `ServerTlsOverride(identity, alpn, clientAuth, trust)` per ClientHello |
| `sessionTickets` | `SessionTicketConfig` | `SessionTicketConfig.Default` | see below | 0.2.0 | the keys and lifetime of a TLS-over-TCP server's tickets and of a QUIC server with `earlyData` (the only QUIC servers that issue tickets) |
| `keylog` (*delicate*) | `KeylogSink?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | TLS secrets as RFC 9850 key log lines ([Key logging](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#key-logging)) |
| `handshakeTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | positive (`Duration.INFINITE`: no deadline) | 0.2.0 | TLS over TCP only (QUIC uses `QuicConfig.handshakeTimeout`) |
| `genericAlerts` | `Boolean` | `false` |  | 0.2.0 | send `handshake_failure` instead of the specific alert |

#### SessionTicketConfig

`SessionTicketConfig(keys, rotateEvery, ticketLifetime)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` (constructor) | `List<ByteArray>?` | `null` (generated in the process) | 1 to 64 entries of 80 bytes | 0.2.0 | explicit ticket keys, shared by the servers of one fleet |
| `rotateEvery` | `Duration` | 1 day | positive, at most 7 days | 0.2.0 | how often the active ticket key is replaced |
| `ticketLifetime` | `Duration` | 12 hours | at least 1 s, at most `rotateEvery / 2` | 0.2.0 | how long a ticket stays valid |

The keys stay in native memory: generated keys never reach Kotlin, explicit keys are
copied there when the configuration is built and the given arrays are zeroed (keep the keys in your secret store, not
in the arrays).

Key exchange groups are not configurable: `X25519MLKEM768`, `X25519`, `secp256r1`, `X448`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`
([Key exchange groups](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#key-exchange-groups)).

### TrustConfig

Guide: [TLS: Trust](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#trust).

| Variant | Parameters (defaults) | Checks | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TrustConfig.Platform` | | Linux Native: a CA store must exist when the client config is built | the operating system's verifier ([Platform trust](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/tls.md#platform-trust)) |
| `TrustConfig.AnchoredCa(roots)` | `roots: List<Certificate>` | at least one root | only these roots, verified inside `ksl`; the only trust for client certificates |
| `TrustConfig.ExpectedName(name, base)` | `base = Platform` | non-blank `name`; `base` is `Platform`, `AnchoredCa` or `Custom` | verify another name than the one connected to (proxies) |
| `TrustConfig.Pinned(pins, scope, base)` | `scope = PinScope.Leaf`, `base = Platform` | at least one pin; not around `Tofu`, `Custom` or another `Pinned` | SPKI pins checked on top of `base`; `PinScope.AnyInValidatedChain` matches any certificate of the validated chain |
| `TrustConfig.Tofu(store)` | `store: TofuStore` | clients only | trust on first use |
| `TrustConfig.Custom(verifier)` (*delicate*) | `verifier: CertificateVerifier` | clients only | your verifier decides; the name check still runs |
| `TrustConfig.fromTrustManager(trustManager)` | | JVM only | a `javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager` as a verifier |

Pins are written `SpkiSha256.parse("sha256/<base64>")` (32 bytes). Certificates come from `Certificate.parsePem` or
DER.

### Identities and key logging

| API | Parameters (defaults) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `TlsIdentity.fromPem(chainPem, keyPem, password)` | `password = null` (encrypted keys are refused) | chain plus one PKCS#8 key; `keyPem` is zeroed and the key lives in OpenSSL only |
| `TlsIdentity.fromDer(chain, keyDer)` | | the same from DER; `keyDer` is zeroed |
| `TlsIdentity.fromKeyStore(keyStore, alias, password)`, `fromPkcs12(bytes, password)` | | JVM only |
| `keylogFile(path)` (*delicate*) | | a 0600 key log file, refused for links, foreign owners and file systems without POSIX permissions |
| `keylogFile(context, name)` (Android, *delicate*) | `name = "kuicksilver-keylog.txt"` | in the app's files; `null` in a non-debuggable build |
| `keylogFromEnvironment()` (*delicate*) | | `SSLKEYLOGFILE`, read only when called |

### Http3Settings

`http3Settings { }` (`Http3Settings.Builder`), `Http3Settings.Default`, `toBuilder()`. Guide: [HTTP/3](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/http3.md).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qpackMaxTableCapacity` | `Long` | 0 | 0..2^30 | 0.2.0 | `SETTINGS_QPACK_MAX_TABLE_CAPACITY` we advertise: the dynamic table the peer's encoder may use |
| `qpackBlockedStreams` | `Long` | 0 | 0..65 535 | 0.2.0 | `SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS` we advertise |
| `encoderMaxTableCapacity` | `Long` | 4096 | 0..2^30 | 0.2.0 | ceiling of our own encoder's dynamic table, under what the peer allows |
| `maxFieldSectionSize` | `Long` | 65 536 (64 KiB) | 1..2^30 | 0.2.0 | largest decoded header or trailer section we accept (and so the longest single field; above it: 431, the connection lives), advertised as `SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE` |
| `enableConnectProtocol` | `Boolean` | `false` |  | 0.2.0 | advertise Extended CONNECT (RFC 9220) |
| `h3Datagram` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | `SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM` (always sent); `Http3Endpoint` sends 0 when `QuicConfig.maxDatagramFrameSize` is 0 |
| `webTransport` | `Boolean` | `false` | needs `enableConnectProtocol` and `h3Datagram` | 0.3.0 | experimental: WebTransport over HTTP/3 (draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-16, with the draft-02 and draft-14 SETTINGS browsers use); `Http3Endpoint.bind` refuses it when `QuicConfig.maxDatagramFrameSize` is 0 |
| `grease` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | send a reserved setting, frame and stream type |
| `maxInformationalResponses` | `Int` | 5 | at least 0 | 0.2.0 | deprecated and ignored since 0.2.1: a client accepts any number of 1xx responses (RFC 9110 section 15.2); their fields together are bounded by `maxFieldSectionSize`, past which the request fails with `H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD` |
| `maxEarlyPriorityUpdates` | `Int` | 32 | at least 0 | 0.2.0 | PRIORITY_UPDATE frames remembered for streams not yet open |
| `glitchProtection` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.2.0 | close with `H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD` a peer that floods useless frames |
| `earlyData` (*experimental*) | `Http3EarlyDataPolicy` | `WaitForHandshake()` | `WaitForHandshake(replayable)`, `Reject425(replayable)`; `replayable` admits GET, HEAD and OPTIONS by default | 0.2.0 | server: what happens to requests that arrive in 0-RTT ([HTTP/3 0-RTT](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/http3.md#0-rtt-opt-in-experimental)) |

`enableQpackDynamicTable()` sets `qpackMaxTableCapacity = 4096` and `qpackBlockedStreams = 16`.

Endpoint and request parameters:

| API | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `Http3Endpoint.bind(local, config, settings)` | `config = QuicEndpointConfig.Default`, `settings = Http3Settings.Default`; the server's TLS must offer ALPN `h3` |
| `Http3Endpoint.connect(remote, tls, quic, settings)` | `quic = QuicConfig.Default`, `settings = Http3Settings.Default`; `tls` must offer ALPN `h3` |
| `Http3Endpoint.connectEarly(remote, tls, quic, settings, earlyData)` (*experimental*) | as `connect`, `earlyData = EarlyDataState.Allowed` (not `Disabled`) |
| `Http3Endpoint.shutdown(grace, code, reason)` (*experimental*) | `code = H3_NO_ERROR`, `reason = "shutdown"` |
| `http3Request(method, authority, path) { ... }` (`Http3Request.Builder`) | `scheme = "https"`, `headers = Http3Headers.Empty`, `body = null` (no body), `trailers = null`, `priority = null` (the default `u=3`), `protocol = null`, `onInformational = null`, `allowEarlyData = false` (*experimental*; GET, HEAD and OPTIONS without a body only) |

#### CapsuleConfig (*experimental*)

How an Extended CONNECT stream speaks the Capsule Protocol (RFC 9297 section 3) once
`Http3Stream.useCapsuleProtocol(config)` is called: the constructor, `capsuleConfig { }` (`CapsuleConfig.Builder`),
`toBuilder()`. Guide: [HTTP/3, capsules](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/http3.md#capsules-experimental).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `knownTypes` | `Set<Long>` | empty | each 0..2^62-1 | 0.3.0 | capsule types delivered in `CapsuleStream.capsules`; other types are skipped as their bytes arrive. DATAGRAM (0x00) always goes to `datagrams` |
| `maxCapsuleLength` | `Int` (bytes) | 65 536 (64 KiB) | 1..1 048 576 | 0.3.0 | longest capsule of a known type; a longer one resets and stops the stream with `H3_MESSAGE_ERROR` |
| `maxDatagramLength` | `Int` (bytes) | 65 536 (64 KiB) | 1..1 048 576 | 0.3.0 | longest DATAGRAM capsule; a longer one is dropped without being buffered |
| `datagramFallback` | `Boolean` | `true` |  | 0.3.0 | send datagrams as DATAGRAM capsules when HTTP/3 datagrams are unsupported (either side's `SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM` is 0, or the peer's SETTINGS have not arrived yet); a datagram too large for QUIC never falls back |
| `receiveQueue` | `Int` | 16 | 1..4096 | 0.3.0 | received capsules held for the collector; when full, reading the stream pauses (flow control holds the peer back) |
| `sendQueue` | `Int` | 32 | 1..4096 | 0.3.0 | capsules waiting to be written; when full, `send` suspends and a fallback `trySendDatagram` answers `QueueFull` |
| `terminalTypes` | `Set<Long>` | empty | among `knownTypes`, not DATAGRAM | 0.3.0 | a capsule of such a type must be the stream's last: it is delivered, and any byte after it resets the stream with `H3_MESSAGE_ERROR` (WebTransport's WT_CLOSE_SESSION) |

### Http2Settings

`Http2Settings(...)` (*experimental*, constructor parameters, immutable). Used by the Ktor client (`http2 { settings = … }`) and
server (`http2Settings = …`); a bad value throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the object is built. Guide: [Ktor: HTTP/2 on
the client](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http2-on-the-client), [on the server](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http2-on-the-server); limits against floods: threat model 3.23.

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `headerTableSize` | `Int` | 4096 | 0..65 536 | 0.3.0 | `SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE`: the HPACK dynamic table the peer may use towards us |
| `maxConcurrentStreams` | `Int` | 100 | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS`: streams the peer may have open towards us; a stream the peer reset still counts until its handler has finished |
| `initialStreamWindow` | `Int` (bytes) | 524 288 (512 KiB) | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | `SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE`: the receive window each stream starts with |
| `maxStreamWindow` | `Int` (bytes) | 6 291 456 (6 MiB) | at least `initialStreamWindow` | 0.3.0 | the largest a stream's receive window grows to while the application reads faster than the window |
| `initialConnectionWindow` | `Int` (bytes) | 786 432 (768 KiB) | at least 65 535 | 0.3.0 | the connection's receive window |
| `maxConnectionWindow` | `Int` (bytes) | 15 728 640 (15 MiB) | at least `initialConnectionWindow` | 0.3.0 | the largest the connection's receive window grows to |
| `maxFrameSize` | `Int` (bytes) | 16 384 | 16 384..16 777 215 | 0.3.0 | `SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE`: the largest frame payload we accept |
| `maxHeaderListSize` | `Int` (bytes) | 65 536 (64 KiB) | 1..2^30 - 1 | 0.3.0 | `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE`: the largest field section we decode (name + value + 32 per field); a larger one fails only its stream, its compressed form is buffered up to twice this, beyond that the connection ends |
| `settingsAckTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | positive | 0.3.0 | how long our SETTINGS may go unacknowledged before the connection ends with `SETTINGS_TIMEOUT` |
| `maxContinuationFrames` | `Int` | 8 | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | CONTINUATION frames allowed in one field block; more ends the connection (`ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM`) |
| `maxControlFramesQueued` | `Int` | 10 000 | at least 1 | 0.3.0 | control frames (SETTINGS and PING acknowledgements, RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE) queued for the peer |
| `maxEmptyFrames` | `Int` | 100 | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | DATA frames in a row with no content and no END_STREAM; more ends the connection |
| `resetBurst` | `Int` | 1000 | at least 1 | 0.3.0 | a server's budget for the client's RST_STREAM frames (Rapid Reset), burst (as nghttp2) |
| `resetsPerSecond` | `Int` | 33 | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | refill rate of that budget per second; 0: it never refills |
| `maxHeaderBlockTime` | `Duration` | 10 s | positive | 0.3.0 | how long one field block (HEADERS and its CONTINUATION frames) may take to arrive |
| `glitchBurst` | `Int` | 10 000 | at least 1 | 0.3.0 | burst of the glitch budget (PRIORITY, unknown frame types, SETTINGS, empty DATA, an unanswered-data PING, every stream error the peer causes) |
| `glitchesPerSecond` | `Int` | 330 | at least 0 | 0.3.0 | refill rate of the glitch budget per second; 0: it never refills |

### Ktor client engine

`HttpClient(Kuicksilver) { engine { … } }` (`KuicksilverEngineConfig`). Values are checked when the engine is created.
Guide: [Ktor: Client](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#client).

| Option | Type | Default | Range | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trust` | `TrustConfig` | `TrustConfig.Platform` |  | 0.2.0 | server verification for HTTP/3, HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 alike |
| `identity` | `TlsIdentity?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | client certificate |
| `tls` | `TlsConfig.Builder.() -> Unit` | `{}` |  | 0.2.0 | further TLS settings, applied after `trust` and `identity` (which it can therefore replace); `alpn` and `serverName` come from the request and are set after it, so the block cannot change them (use `TrustConfig.ExpectedName` to verify another name) |
| `quic` | `QuicConfig` | `QuicConfig.Default` | its `connectionIdLength` and `http3.endpoint.connectionIdLength` agree: the one left at 8 follows the other; two different explicit values fail the engine's creation | 0.2.0 | QUIC transport of HTTP/3 connections |
| `maxIdleConnectionsPerRoute` | `Int` | 4 | at least 0 | 0.2.0 | idle HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections kept per route; not a connection limit |
| `maxConnectionsCount` (*experimental*) | `Int` | 1000 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | TCP connections (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2) of the engine, idle ones included; requests beyond it wait (FIFO, within the connect timeout) |
| `maxConnectionsPerRoute` (*experimental*) | `Int` | 100 | at least 1 | 0.2.0 | TCP connections to one route (scheme, host, port, proxy); an HTTP/2 connection counts once however many requests it carries |
| `idleTimeout` (*experimental*) | `Duration` | 5 min | positive | 0.2.0 | idle HTTP/1.1 connections, and HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 connections without requests, are closed after this |
| `maxConnectionLifetime` (*experimental*) | `Duration` | infinite | positive | 0.2.0 | age after which a connection takes no new requests |
| `connectTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s |  | 0.2.0 | connect timeout (TCP + TLS, or the QUIC handshake) when `HttpTimeout` sets none; a WebSocket over HTTP/1.1 also waits at most this long for the answer to its opening handshake (`ConnectTimeoutException`) |
| `connectionAttemptDelay` (*experimental*) | `Duration` | 250 ms | 10 ms..2 s, or `Duration.INFINITE`; anything else fails the engine's creation | 0.3.0 | Happy Eyeballs (RFC 8305) for HTTP/1.1's TCP connects: the delay before the next address is tried while earlier attempts are still pending; `INFINITE` tries one address after another ([Ktor: IPv6 over TCP](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#ipv6-over-tcp-on-kotlinnative)) |
| `logger` (*experimental*) | `KuicksilverLogger?` | `null` (keeps `http3.endpoint.logger`) |  | 0.2.0 | the engine's and its QUIC endpoint's diagnostics |
| `eventListener` (*experimental*) | `KuicksilverEventListener?` | `null` |  | 0.2.0 | call, protocol, race, Alt-Svc and pool events ([Ktor: Observability](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#observability-experimental)) |
| `proxy` (Ktor) | `ProxyConfig?` | `null` | HTTP (`http://` only) and SOCKS5 proxies; others, an `https://` proxy URL included, fail each request with `UnsupportedOperationException` | 0.2.0 | TCP through the proxy (HTTP/1.1, or HTTP/2 inside the tunnel) (CONNECT for `https` and WebSockets, absolute form for `http`; SOCKS5 CONNECT with the proxy resolving names); HTTP/3 is never proxied |
| `proxyResolver` (*experimental*) | `ProxyResolver` | `ProxyResolvers.System` | `System`, `Environment`, `None` or your own | 0.3.0 | the proxy for requests `proxy` does not cover, per scheme, host and port (kept 30 s); each lookup is bounded by the engine's `connectTimeout` (not a per-request `HttpTimeout`) and fails the request with `ProxyException` beyond it; loopback is always direct with the built-ins; docs/guide/ktor.md, "Proxies" |
| `proxyCredentials` (*experimental*) | `ProxyCredentials?` | `null` | SOCKS5: user 1–255 bytes, password up to 255 (RFC 1929) | 0.3.0 | for the explicit `proxy` only (a resolver's proxy carries its own `ResolvedProxy.credentials`); SOCKS5 username/password when the proxy picks it; `Proxy-Authorization: Basic` on an HTTP proxy's CONNECT and absolute-form requests unless the request has its own; off the JVM the proxy URL's user info wins |

`pipelining` (from Ktor's `HttpClientEngineConfig`) is not used.

#### HTTP/2 client options

`http2 { … }` (`Http2ClientConfig`, *experimental*; guide: [HTTP/2 on the client](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http2-on-the-client)):

| Option | Type | Default | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `Boolean` | `true` | 0.3.0 | offer `h2` and `http/1.1` in ALPN on every `https://` connection over TCP (not WebSockets); `false` offers only `http/1.1`, as in 0.2 |
| `settings` | `Http2Settings` | `Http2Settings()` | 0.3.0 | our SETTINGS, windows (512 KiB per stream growing to 6 MiB, 768 KiB per connection growing to 15 MiB) and the limits held against the server (64 KiB field sections, 10 s for our SETTINGS to be acknowledged, the flood limits; threat model 3.23) |
| `pingInterval` | `Duration` | `Duration.INFINITE` | 0.3.0 | a PING this often on every HTTP/2 connection; one still unanswered at the next ends the connection and fails its calls; at least 100 ms, else the engine's creation fails with `IllegalArgumentException` |

#### HTTP/3 client options

`http3 { … }` (`Http3ClientConfig`; guide: [HTTP/3 on the client](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#http3-on-the-client)):

| Option | Type | Default | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery` | `Http3DiscoveryMode` | `Auto` | 0.2.0 | `Auto` (TCP first, HTTP/3 after `Alt-Svc`), `Preferred` (HTTP/3 first, TCP fallback), `H3Only`, `H1Only` (no HTTP/3; TCP is HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2) |
| `quicHints` | `Set<HostPort>` | empty | 0.2.0 | origins treated as `Preferred` in `Auto` mode; `HostPort(host, port)` compares the host exactly as in URLs |
| `altSvcStore` | `AltSvcStore` | `InMemoryAltSvcStore()` | 0.2.0 | where alternatives live; `FileAltSvcStore(path)` keeps them across restarts |
| `clearOnNetworkChange` | `Boolean` | `true` | 0.2.0 | drop alternatives without `persist=1` when `networkId` changes (RFC 7838 section 2.2); `false` keeps them |
| `httpsRecords` (*experimental*) | `HttpsRecordSource` | `HttpsRecordSource.Off` | 0.3.0 | HTTPS resource records (RFC 9460) as a source of HTTP/3 in `Auto`: `System` (the OS resolver) or `Exchange { query -> response }` (your DNS-over-HTTPS client) ([HTTPS records](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#https-records-experimental)) |
| `httpsRecordExtraWait` (*experimental*) | `Duration` | 50 ms | 0.3.0 | how long a request waits for the HTTPS records after the origin's addresses resolved; 50 ms (RFC 9460 section 5.1) to 1 s, else the engine's creation fails with `IllegalArgumentException` |
| `hardDelay` | `Duration?` | `null` (1.5 x the origin's smoothed RTT, 250 ms without history, clamped to 100 ms..2 s) | 0.2.0 | head start of HTTP/3 over HTTP/1.1 in a race on a network where QUIC was confirmed (10 ms elsewhere); an explicit value must be 10 ms..2 s or `Duration.INFINITE` (RFC 8305 section 5; INFINITE starts HTTP/1.1 only after HTTP/3 failed, on every network), else the engine's creation fails with `IllegalArgumentException` |
| `networkId` | `() -> String?` | `{ null }` (one network) | 0.2.0 | identifies the current network; a change forgets broken marks, QUIC confirmation and HTTPS records; the engine caches HTTPS records only when it is set |
| `settings` | `Http3Settings` | `Http3Settings.Default` | 0.2.0 | HTTP/3 settings of the engine's connections |
| `endpoint` | `QuicEndpointConfig` | `QuicEndpointConfig.Default` | 0.2.0 | the client QUIC endpoint (bound to `0.0.0.0:0`, a dual-stack socket on the accelerated transport) |
| `earlyData` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `false` | 0.2.0 | 0-RTT for GET, HEAD and OPTIONS without a body on resumed connections |
| `qlog` (*experimental*) | `QlogSink?` | `null` (keeps `quic.qlog`) | 0.2.0 | a qlog trace per HTTP/3 connection |
| `connectionListener` (*experimental*) | `ConnectionListener?` | `null` (keeps `endpoint.listener`) | 0.2.0 | lifecycle of every QUIC connection |
| `webTransportIgnoresProxy` (*experimental*) | `Boolean` | `false` | 0.3.0 | `HttpClient.webTransport` connects directly although a proxy applies to the URL; otherwise such a call fails with `UnsupportedOperationException` ([WebTransport on the client](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#webtransport-on-the-client-experimental)) |
| `maxWebTransportSessions` (*experimental*) | `Int` | 64 | 0.3.0 | WebTransport sessions open at once, each on its own QUIC connection; at least 1; one more fails at once with `IllegalStateException` |
| `http3Allowed` (*experimental*) | `() -> Boolean` | `{ true }` | 0.3.0 | kill switch read once per `https://` request and `webTransport` call (not with `H1Only`): false sends a request over TCP, HTTP/2 included (`H3Only` requests and `webTransport` fail with `UnsupportedOperationException`); a switch that throws an exception allows HTTP/3 and is logged at most once per 5 minutes ([Turning HTTP/3 off remotely](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#turning-http3-off-remotely)) |
| `diagnosticsLogLevel` (*experimental*) | `LogLevel?` | `Info` | 0.3.0 | level of the engine logger's line for a call HTTP/3 could have served but did not; calls over HTTP/3 or never meant for it are logged at `Debug`; `null` writes none ([Why did this request not use HTTP/3?](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#why-did-this-request-not-use-http3)) |
| `connectionMigration` (*experimental*) | `Http3ConnectionMigration?` | `null` (connections stay on the network they were opened on) | 0.3.0 | pooled HTTP/3 connections follow the network (RFC 9000 section 9); `Http3ConnectionMigration.followDefaultNetwork(connectivity)` on Android, `followDefaultNetwork()` on iOS and macOS, your own `NetworkMigrator` elsewhere; events go to `connectionMigrated` ([Connection migration](https://github.com/kuicksilver/kuicksilver/blob/main/docs/guide/ktor.md#connection-migration)) |

### Ktor server engine
